value: oleic acid gave a strong repellent activity against both sexes in the laboratory ambulatory assay; hexane repelled the males
method: laboratory choice arena: wooden chamber 150 x 10 x 10 cm in fifteen sections, compound on a cotton swab at one end, distribution of walking beetles recorded on video; 50 beetles of one sex per compound per day
conditions: adults collected by Barber pitfall traps in forest around Kaunas, Lithuania, then kept in the laboratory; 40 compounds and mixtures tested; each compound tested once a day with 50 males or 50 females; the Results give no test statistics; the page mentions no control arena

source.authors: Faly L, Brygadyrenko V, Paulauskas A
source.title: Repellent and Attractant Activities of Organic Compounds on Female and Male Philonthus decorus (Coleoptera, Staphylinidae)

quote: A strong repellent activity against both sexes of Ph. decorus was caused by oleic acid, while hexane repelled the males.
note: Same paper, qualifying the abstract: Results say 'Hexane was a strong repellent against the males and was neutral to the females' and call oleic acid 'High repellent activity against both sexes'; the abstract also says females were in general less sensitive and that the rest of the 40 compounds caused no ambulatory response. Effects are the authors' qualitative scale with no printed statistic. Licence: the page prints no licence sentence and its metadata lists CC BY 3.0; Crossref gives CC BY 4.0, vor, start 2024-04-25 (CC BY 3.0 page versus CC BY 4.0 Crossref). Name authority (GBIF, CoL) refused or not reached: taxon name unchecked; family and order from the genus placement printed in the title. Chemical avoidance in a walking assay: no receptor or sense organ is identified.

value: a female responded in 65 of 120 playback tests of a synthesized male calling signal (MCaS) played back on single tea leaves
method: playback of a synthesized signal built from a pre-recorded MCaS unit (1.491 s, dominant frequency 340.8 Hz) repeated to a 5 min signal, played on the second, fourth, sixth, seventh, eighth and tenth leaves under the bud of 20 tea branches while a female sat on the seventh leaf; a new female for each test
conditions: adults collected at the Tea Research Institute, Hangzhou, China, in 2023 and 2024; the paper gives no explicit definition of a female response (female signals on her leaf were recorded)

source.authors: Shan Y, Yao Q, Jia Q, Lu J, Cai X, Chen Z, Bian L
source.title: The Effect of Leaf Traits on the Excitation, Transmission, and Perception of Vibrational Mating Signals in the Tea Leafhopper Empoasca onukii Matsuda (Hemiptera: Cicadellidae)

quote: A total of 65 females responded to the MCaS playback out of a total of 120 tests performed.
note: Null in the same paper: 'none of the MCaS parameters affected female responses (p > 0.05' (whether a female responded); the Results give no response frequency by playback leaf. The paper names the species Empoasca onukii; the repository's GBIF name list gives Empoasca onukii as a SYNONYM of Matsumurasca onukii, so the accepted name is used here (other authorities not reached). Licence: the page prints no full licence sentence (metadata lists CC BY 3.0); Crossref gives CC BY 4.0, vor, start 2025-04-07. MCaS is the paper's abbreviation for the male calling signal; playback is of a synthesized signal, not of live males.

value: the light-startle response, and habituation of it, occurs when lights are turned on and when lights are turned off
method: Experiment 1: startle response of individual cockroaches to room lights switched on or off across repeated trials, n = 96 cockroaches
conditions: laboratory colony bred from commercial-supplier founders (not wild-caught); Experiment 1 stimulus four fluorescent room lights (32 W, 2196 lumens each) with two 3 W red bulbs for illumination; light-on and light-off trials compared; light colour of the later flashlight stimulus not stated

source.title: Habituation of the Light-Startle Response of Orange Head Cockroaches (Eublaberus posticus): Effects of Acclimation, Stimulus Duration, Presence of Food, and Intertrial Interval

where: Abstract, sentence returned in two consecutive pieces and joined
quote: In our first experiment, we found that LSR, and habituation of LSR, occurs to both lights being turned on and lights being turned off.
note: LSR is the paper's abbreviation for light-startle response. Qualifiers in the same paper: Experiment 1 Results give overall response probability lower for light-on trials (estimate = -1.918, p = 0.005) and lower for subjects with a light-on acclimation period (estimate = -2.839, p < 0.000); Experiment 2 (stimulus 2, 4, 8 or 10 s, 100-lumen flashlight) found that light duration did not affect response. Whole-field light change with no wavelength or eye-specific test, so no spectral or visual-organ claim. Licence: page prints no licence sentence (metadata lists CC BY 3.0); Crossref gives CC BY 4.0, vor, start 2021-04-11. Name authority not reached: taxon name unchecked.
